summary: Washington County, ME wood tower 1913, rebuilt 1925; steel tower of salvaged steel 1937; index lists it gone, removal planned in 2008 report, date not found.

facts.design: wood fire watch tower (1913, rebuilt 1925), replaced in 1937 by a non-standard steel tower of salvaged materials, using steel from the Naval Radio Tower in Bar Harbor
facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association Maine list marks it gone; the 2008 Maine chapter report still called removal necessary; no removal date found in sources read

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts lists the same 1913, 1925 and 1937 history under Cooper Mountain #37. The dates match Maine Memory's Cooper Hill record, so the two names probably refer to one lookout; no source states this outright.

A Facebook post by the Maine chapter says the tower was removed in 2008, but it could not be read or quoted. The 2008 chapter report calls the removal a future plan, and the 2009 and 2010 chapter reports list no Cooper Hill removal. The year is left unresolved.

notes_for_editor: Removal year unresolved. The Facebook posts by the FFLA Maine chapter ('removed in 2008 to make way for a radio tower installation') could not be read by fetch_text (title only), so they are not cited. The 2009 report (cr-me-2009.pdf) has no Cooper match; the 2010 report's 2011 planned-removal list does not include Cooper Hill. Identity with Cooper Mountain #37 is inferred from identical 1913/1925/1937 dates. No photo URL was found; the Maine Memory record gives only a page link.
